description:
Sampling 5 crates with `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-W missing_docs" cargo doc -p <crate> --no-deps`:

| Crate | missing_docs warnings |
|---|---|
| jmap-types | 5 (enum variants) |
| jmap-mail-types | 71 (all enum variants in backend.rs Property enums) |
| jmap-mail-server | 0 |
| jmap-mail-client | 41 (32 struct fields + 8 modules + 1 crate-level) |
| jmap-mime | 0 |

Full-workspace count likely exceeds 200. The bulk is the spec-defined Property enum variants: `MailboxProperty::{Id, Name, ParentId, Role, …}`, `EmailProperty::{...}`, etc. — all are RFC 8621 §2/§4 named identifiers and could be documented from the RFC text in a single sweep.

`jmap-mail-client` has structurally weaker coverage: missing crate-level docstring, missing module docs on every method module, undocumented response-struct fields (`account_id`, `state`, `list`, `not_found`).

Suggested phased approach:
1. Add `#![warn(missing_docs)]` at each crate root (so warnings keep accumulating until fixed)
2. Add crate-level docstrings to client crates
3. Document Property enum variants (mechanical sweep, can be a single agent task)
4. Eventually upgrade to `#![deny(missing_docs)]` for type crates

This is a marathon, not a sprint — a P2 because partial coverage is acceptable for v0.1, but the missing variants leak through to docs.rs and look unfinished.
title: P2: missing_docs at scale on type-crate enum variants (117+ in 5 sampled crates)
